title: Tame trait quotient and change of logarithmic base
statement:
A trait is $\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal. It is complete strictly henselian if $R$ is complete for that ideal, is henselian (simple roots of monic polynomials over its residue field lift), and has separably closed residue field. Its canonical log structure is $\mathcal O\cap j_*\mathcal O_\eta^\times$, where $j$ includes its generic point. Mixed characteristic means fraction-field characteristic zero and positive residue characteristic.

Let $S^{\prime}\to S$ be a finite dominant extension of complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic traits. Let a finite group $H$ act on $S^{\prime}$ over $S$, with $\#H$ invertible on $S$. Put $R^{\prime}=\Gamma(S^{\prime},\mathcal O_{S^{\prime}})$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}((R^{\prime})^H)$, where $(R^{\prime})^H=\{r:h(r)=r\text{ for all }h\in H\}$. Then $T$ is a complete strictly henselian trait, $T\to S$ is finite dominant, and $S^{\prime}\to T$ is finite dominant and log etale for the canonical fs log structures [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale, def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Its generic-field degree divides $\#H$, allowing a nonfaithful action. For every locally Noetherian fs log scheme $V$ log smooth over $S^{\prime}$, the composite $V\to T$ is log smooth. Here finite means affine with module-finite coordinate algebras [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and dominant means having dense image.

source.place: Expose XVI 3.7, p.254, sentences from T=S prime/H through log smoothness over T; Expose VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72, for tame Kummer charts.

proof.text: Write $B=R^{\prime}$, $L=\operatorname{Frac}B$ and $A=B^H$. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], the rings of both given traits are DVRs; use the normalized additive valuation $v:L^\times\to\mathbf Z$ of $B$, so $B=\{0\}\cup\{x:v(x)\geq0\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], $B$ is integral over $R$; the maximal-preimage clause of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-algebra-ideal-in-radical] (with $I=0$) shows that its maximal ideal contracts to the unique maximal ideal of $R$. Thus a uniformizer of $R$ has positive value in $B$. Each $h$ extends to $L$ by $h(a/b)=h(a)/h(b)$. Let $G$ be the image of $H$ in $\operatorname{Aut}(L)$ and put $F=L^G$. The action of $G$ is faithful. Apply [lem-wf-finite-field-action-fixed-degree]: $L/F$ is finite Galois of degree $d=|G|$. The fibres of $H\twoheadrightarrow G$ are cosets of its kernel, all of the same size, so $d\mid\#H$. If $p>0$ is the residue characteristic of $R$, the unit hypothesis on $\#H$ implies $p\nmid d$.

eq1}h(b)\in B\cap F=A$. Restrict $v$ to $F^	imes$. Its image is a nonzero subgroup of $\mathbf Z$, since a uniformizer of $R$ has positive value in $B$ (as checked in Step 1). Write this subgroup as $r\mathbf Z$, $r>0$, and choose $\pi\in F$ with $v(\pi)=r$. Then $\pi\in A$. Elements of value zero are precisely the units of $A$; for every nonzero ideal $J$ of $A$, choose an element $a\in J$ of least value. Every $b\in J$ has $v(b/a)\geq0$, so $b/a\in A$ and $J=aA$. Thus $A$ is local, every ideal is principal, and $\pi$ generates its nonzero maximal ideal. It is a DVR, hence a trait, by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. This is a direct valuation argument, not a new invariant-ring lemma.

proof.text: Since $R$ is Noetherian and $B$ is finite over $R$, the $R$-submodule $A\subset B$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. The same finite list of $R$-module generators of $B$ generates it over $A$, since $R\subset A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product] to $R\to A$: as $A$ is a domain it is complete for its maximal ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting] ((ii)$\Rightarrow$(i)), the root-lifting henselianity of $R$ in the statement is henselianity in the idempotent sense of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product]; apply that node to the same map. A nonzero domain has no nontrivial idempotent, so only one factor occurs; $A$ is henselian and its residue field $k_A$ is finite over $k_R$; by (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting], simple roots of monic polynomials over $k_A$ lift to $A$, as the statement's definition requires. By [lem-kun-sep-closed-finite-extension-sep-closed], $k_A$ is separably closed. Thus $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is complete strictly henselian. Both $R\hookrightarrow A$ and $A\hookrightarrow B$ are module-finite and injective, so the two scheme maps are finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and dominant: the zero prime maps to the zero prime, whose closure in either domain spectrum is the whole spectrum. The embeddings also preserve characteristic zero and the positive residue characteristic.

source.place: Tags 00IK, lemma-Noetherian-basic; 0325, lemma-quotient-complete-local; 04GH, lemma-finite-over-henselian; fields.tex Tag 030K, lemma-separable-first

proof.text: The DVRs $A$ and $B$ are normal by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Since $B$ is finite over $A$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] says its elements are integral over $A$. Conversely, an element of $L$ integral over $A$ is integral over $B$ by the same monic equation, and belongs to $B$ by its normality. Thus $B$ is exactly the integral closure of $A$ in $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field], $\operatorname{Gal}(L/F)$ has order $[L:F]=d$. The image $G$ is a subgroup of this automorphism group of the same order, so it is the whole group. Every such automorphism preserves $B$ (apply it to monic equations over $A$), hence its unique maximal ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product], $k_B/k_A$ is finite; by [lem-kun-sep-closed-finite-extension-purely-inseparable] it is purely inseparable. Every $k_A$-automorphism of $k_B$ is therefore the identity: if $x^{p^m}\in k_A$, the equation $X^{p^m}=x^{p^m}$ has at most one root. Consequently both decomposition and inertia groups are the whole $G$.

source.place: Tags 09E8, remark-finite-separable-extension; 09EE, lemma-galois-inertia; algebra.tex Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral; fields.tex Tag 09I1, lemma-finite-Galois

proof.text: Choose uniformizers $\pi\in A$ and $w\in B$, and write $\pi=uw^e$ with $u\in B^\times$. By [lem-exc-dvr-galois-degree-data], $d=e f$, where $f=[k_B:k_A]$; the number of maximal ideals is one since $B$ is local. Thus $e$ is prime to $p$. Apply [lem-exc-finite-dvr-tame-inertia] to the now verified integral closure $B/A$ and finite Galois extension $L/F$. Its wild kernel $P\subset I=G$ is a finite $p$-group, while $|G|=d$ is prime to $p$, so $P=1$ (coset counting makes $|P|$ divide $d$). Its tame quotient has order the prime-to-$p$ part of $e$, which here is $e$ itself. Hence $d=|G|=|I/P|=e$ and $f=1$. In particular the residue map $k_A\to k_B$ is an isomorphism and $e$ is invertible in both local rings. This establishes total tame ramification without assuming the separably closed residue fields perfect.

The polynomial $X^e-\bar u$ over the separably closed residue field $k_B$ has a root $\bar b$, since $e$ is prime to $p$ and $\bar u\neq0$, so it is separable. Its derivative at that root is $e\bar b^{e-1}\neq0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting], applied in the henselian ring $B$, this root lifts to $b\in B$ with $b^e=u$. Its residue is nonzero, hence $b$ is a unit. Set $t=bw$. It is a uniformizer of $B$ and $t^e=\pi$. The argument includes $e=1$.

source.place: Tag 04GG, lemma-characterize-henselian, simple-root lifting; more-algebra.tex Tag 09EV, tame root-of-uniformizer construction

proof.text: Let $D=A[Z]/(Z^e-\pi)$ and map $Z$ to $t$. By [lem-sbc-dvr-uniformizer-root-algebra], $D$ is a DVR. To check this map injective, reduce a polynomial modulo the monic equation to $\sum_{0\leq i<e}a_iZ^i$. If its image is nonzero termwise, the term values $v(a_it^i)=e v_A(a_i)+i$ are distinct modulo $e$. A term of strictly least value cannot cancel: divide by it; its residue is nonzero and every other summand has residue zero. Thus the kernel is zero. The same calculation with $a_i\in F$ proves the $e$ elements $1,t,\ldots,t^{e-1}$ linearly independent over $F$. Since $[L:F]=e$, they form a basis, so the fraction field of the embedded $D$ is $L$. The DVR $D$ is integrally closed by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Every element of $B$ satisfies a monic equation over $A\subset D$ from Step 4, so lies in $D$. The reverse inclusion holds by construction. We have proved the actual $A$-algebra identification $B=A[t]=A[Z]/(Z^e-\pi)$.

proof.text: The canonical log structures have the uniformizer charts $\mathbf N\to A$, $1\mapsto\pi$, and $\mathbf N\to B$, $1\mapsto t$, as stated in [lem-per-trait-log-smooth-uniformizer-chart]. The map of charts is $1\mapsto e$. Its group map $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z$ has zero kernel and cokernel $\mathbf Z/e\mathbf Z$, of unit order. The underlying comparison $\operatorname{Spec}B\to T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]$ is the identity under the presentation of Step 7. It is etale (an identity is flat, finitely presented and unramified). Therefore [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] gives log etaleness of $S^{\prime}\to T$. These are fs charts since $\mathbf N$ is finitely generated, integral and saturated. Step 1 gives its generic-field degree $e=d\mid\#H$.

source.place: Expose VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72, standard Kummer etale covers; XVI Definition 3.6.1, p.252, canonical uniformizer chart; XVI 3.7, p.254

proof.text: Now let $(V,M_V)\to S^{\prime}$ be the stated log-smooth morphism. At each geometric point apply [lem-per-trait-log-smooth-uniformizer-chart], with the specific uniformizer $t$ constructed above. It supplies an etale neighborhood $U\to V$, an fs monoid $Q$ with torsion-free group completion $Q^{\rm gp}$, an injective $u:\mathbf N\to Q$, and a chart compatible with $1\mapsto t$, for which $C=Q^{\rm gp}/\mathbf Z u(1)$ has finite torsion subgroup of order $n$ invertible on $U$. The comparison $U\to S^{\prime}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$ is etale. The hypotheses of that node are exactly the given locally Noetherian fs condition and log smoothness over a trait; it imposes no regularity or finite-type assumption on $V$. Use for $V\to T$ the same chart on $U$ and the map $\mathbf N\to Q$, $1\mapsto e u(1)$.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3 with the fixed chart Q=N on the base trait, printed p.252

proof.text: Put $q=u(1)$. The group map for the composite chart is injective because $u^{\rm gp}$ is injective and $e>0$. Write $C'=Q^{\rm gp}/\mathbf Z(e q)$. The natural surjection $C'\to C$ has kernel $\mathbf Zq/\mathbf Z(e q)\cong\mathbf Z/e\mathbf Z$. Its inverse image of $C_{\rm tors}$ is exactly $C'_{\rm tors}$: if $m x=a q$ modulo the representatives in $Q^{\rm gp}$, then $emx=0$ in $C'$, and the converse follows by projection. Thus $0\to\mathbf Z/e\mathbf Z\to C'_{\rm tors}\to C_{\rm tors}\to0$ is exact. Each fibre has $e$ elements, so $C'_{\rm tors}$ is finite of order $en$, which is invertible on $U$ since both $e$ and $n$ are. This is an explicit computation of the chart cokernel, not an appeal to logarithmic composition.

source.place: Expose XVI 3.7, p.254, log smoothness over T; chart group calculation using Proposition 3.6.3

proof.text:
The two comparison targets are the same scheme with the same induced map from $U$. Indeed their coordinate algebras are respectively
$$B\otimes_{\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\mathbf Z[Q]
\cong A[Z]\otimes_{\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\mathbf Z[Q]/(Z^e-\pi)
\cong A[Q]/(z^{e q}-\pi)
\cong A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\mathbf Z[Q],$$
where the first tensor uses $1\mapsto t$ and $1\mapsto q$, and the last uses $1\mapsto\pi$ and $1\mapsto e q$. In the middle, $Z$ is identified with $z^q$. The comparison maps agree since they have the same $Q$-chart and $A$-structure map; this calculation takes place on affine opens of the targets and does not require $U$ affine. The comparison for $V\to T$ is therefore the etale comparison of Step 9, hence smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. The charts cover every geometric point of $V$; with the group conditions of Step 10, [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] gives log smoothness of the composite. This proves the last clause and completes the item.
